behaviorChanges: The plan-review deadlock is closed at both ends: a PreToolUse guard blocks editing a source-of-truth plan that a successful capped review run reviewed while no manifest binds the current content (the edit that previously wedged the lane), and the runtime-cap and recovery messages name the sanctioned successor-plan path instead of prescribing the run-plan-review the cap will refuse. The successor-plan practice is now documented policy.

Process authority is write-protected against memory systems: the memory policy module adds the never-write-process-to-memory rule and routes mid-session process lessons through framework-intake (RCA when a control failed, feature request when it is missing); the framework-intake reference adds the post-publication point-only memory rule, a memory-write drift pattern, and the operator-ratified decision-capture-artifact (DCA) vocabulary alias.

optionalMigrations.description: The plan-edit guard hook (blocks the edit that creates the plan-review sha-stale-at-cap deadlock) installs automatically at the next lane-start; run install-hooks now to arm it immediately on lanes with plans mid-review.

requiredMigrations.command: gh auth refresh --hostname github.com -s read:project -s project
requiredMigrations.description: Carried forward from 0.10.3 for lanes updating across it: grant the gh token the GitHub Projects scopes the fail-closed board gates need. Machines already on 0.10.3+ or whose token carries read:project and project need no action.

rollbackNotes: Pinning back to 0.10.4 removes the guard hook at the next hook regeneration and restores the old cap/recovery text; a lane already wedged in the sha-stale-at-cap state regains the misleading run-plan-review instruction, and the successor-plan path keeps working in both directions (it is convention, not machinery).
